title: Key word transformations 1
instructions: For questions 1-6, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between three and six words, including the word given.

questions.original: I had no idea that the meeting had been cancelled.
questions.prompt: _____ the meeting had been cancelled.
questions.explanation: Inversión tras el adverbio restrictivo «little»: «Little did I know (that)...». Tras «little» va el auxiliar «did» + sujeto + infinitivo sin «to».

questions.original: People believe that the thieves escaped through the roof.
questions.prompt: The thieves _____ through the roof.
questions.explanation: Pasiva impersonal con sujeto personal: «sujeto + is/are believed + to have + participio» cuando la acción creída es anterior.

questions.original: "You really should get a second opinion," the engineer told me.
questions.prompt: The engineer _____ a second opinion.
questions.explanation: Verbo de estilo indirecto «advise + objeto + to-infinitivo» (o «advise that + sujeto + (should) + infinitivo»).

questions.original: We only finished on time because the contractors worked through the weekend.
questions.prompt: We would not have finished on time _____ through the weekend.
accepted: if the contractors had not worked
questions.explanation: Tercera condicional sobre un hecho pasado contrario a la realidad. Con inversión se omite «if»: «had the contractors not worked». Ojo: en la inversión no se contrae («hadn't the contractors» es incorrecto).

questions.original: The committee rejected the proposal because it was too expensive.
questions.prompt: The proposal _____ by the committee because of its cost.
questions.explanation: «Turn down» = rechazar. Al pasar a pasiva (el sujeto es «the proposal»): «was turned down by».

questions.original: The new system is nowhere near as efficient as we had hoped.
questions.prompt: The new system is _____ we had hoped.
questions.explanation: «Nowhere near as ... as» equivale a un comparativo de inferioridad reforzado: «far less efficient than». «Far» intensifica el comparativo.

title: Key word transformations 2
instructions: For questions 1-6, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between three and six words, including the word given.

questions.original: The suspect was released only after his lawyer had arrived.
questions.prompt: Not _____ was the suspect released.
questions.explanation: «Not until + oración» al inicio provoca inversión en la oración principal («was the suspect released»).

questions.original: It is possible that the evidence was tampered with before it reached the lab.
questions.prompt: The evidence _____ with before it reached the lab.
questions.explanation: Deducción sobre el pasado en pasiva: «may have been + participio». Se mantiene la preposición «with» del verbo «tamper with».

questions.original: The officer said it was my fault that the accident had happened.
questions.prompt: The officer _____ the accident.
questions.explanation: «Blame somebody for something/doing something» = culpar a alguien de algo. Verbo de estilo indirecto con preposición dependiente «for».

questions.original: Nobody expected the operation to be so successful.
questions.prompt: The success of the operation _____.
questions.explanation: Colocación «exceed (all/everyone's) expectations» = superar las expectativas. Recuerda que «everyone's» cuenta como una sola palabra.

questions.original: The investigation is being hindered by a lack of witnesses.
questions.prompt: A lack of witnesses _____ the investigation.
accepted: is getting in the way of
is standing in the way of
questions.explanation: «Get/stand in the way of» = obstaculizar. Se mantiene el aspecto continuo del original («is being hindered» → «is getting in the way of»).

questions.original: They will have to postpone the trial until the new judge is appointed.
questions.prompt: The trial will have to _____ until the new judge is appointed.
questions.explanation: «Put off» = aplazar. Tras «will have to» la pasiva es «be + participio»: «be put off».

title: Key word transformations 3
instructions: For questions 1-6, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between three and six words, including the word given.

questions.original: The plant manager arranged for someone to replace the faulty valve immediately.
questions.prompt: The plant manager _____ immediately.
questions.explanation: Causativa «have + objeto + participio»: el gerente encargó la tarea a otra persona.

questions.original: Production must not resume before the inspection has been completed, whatever happens.
questions.prompt: Under _____ resume before the inspection has been completed.
questions.explanation: «Under no circumstances» al inicio exige inversión: auxiliar/modal + sujeto («must production resume»).

questions.original: The new regulations will affect small companies more than anyone else.
questions.prompt: The new regulations will _____ small companies than on anyone else.
accepted: have more of an impact on
questions.explanation: Colocación «have an impact on» en comparativo: «have a greater impact on X than on Y». La preposición «on» se repite en el segundo término.

questions.original: It's a pity we didn't carry out a risk assessment before starting.
questions.prompt: I _____ out a risk assessment before starting.
questions.explanation: Lamento sobre el pasado: «wish + past perfect». Se mantiene el phrasal verb «carry out».

questions.original: The supplier said that the delay was not their fault.
questions.prompt: The supplier _____ for the delay.
accepted: denied that they were to blame
questions.explanation: «Deny + -ing» o «deny that...»: negar ser responsable. «Responsible for» y «to blame for» encajan con el «for» de la frase.

questions.original: Costs rose so sharply that the project had to be abandoned.
questions.prompt: There was _____ costs that the project had to be abandoned.
questions.explanation: «So + adverbio» pasa a «such a + adjetivo + sustantivo»: «such a sharp rise in costs that...». «Rise/increase» rigen «in».

title: Key word transformations 4
instructions: For questions 1-6, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between three and six words, including the word given.

questions.original: As soon as the alarm went off, the guards sealed the building.
questions.prompt: No _____ off than the guards sealed the building.
questions.explanation: «No sooner + had + sujeto + participio ... than»: inversión con past perfect. El participio de «go off» es «gone off».

questions.original: I'd prefer you not to mention this to the press.
questions.prompt: I _____ this to the press.
accepted: would rather you did not mention
questions.explanation: «Would rather + sujeto distinto + pasado simple» expresa preferencia sobre lo que hace otra persona en el presente o futuro.

questions.original: Everyone says the new chief inspector is extremely competent.
questions.prompt: The new chief inspector _____ extremely competent.
questions.explanation: «Have a reputation for/of being + adjetivo» = tener fama de. Tras preposición, gerundio («being»).

questions.original: The witness was so frightened that she could not speak.
questions.prompt: The witness _____ speak.
questions.explanation: «So + adjetivo + that ... could not» equivale a «too + adjetivo + to-infinitivo».

questions.original: It wasn't necessary for you to call an ambulance, but you did.
questions.prompt: You _____ an ambulance.
questions.explanation: «Needn't have + participio» indica que algo se hizo pero no era necesario. «Didn't need to call» no transmite que la acción sí se realizó, por eso no se acepta aquí.

questions.original: The minister's announcement took the journalists completely by surprise.
questions.prompt: The journalists _____ by the minister's announcement.
questions.explanation: «Be taken aback (by)» = quedarse desconcertado. Hay que conservar el intensificador «completely» y usar la pasiva.
